newsitem.title: INDIA: India Tatas mull fate of blocked SIA deal.
newsitem.headline: India Tatas mull fate of blocked SIA deal.

text.p: India's Tata Industries will seek ways to rescue a $600 million tie-up with Singapore Airlines in the domestic sector following a federal decision that effectively blocked the deal, a company official said on Wednesday.
Prime H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet on Tuesday forbade foreign airlines from holding equity in the domestic sector, in a move which appears to rule out the deal between the Tatas and SIA.
"We can only say we are very disappointed," Tata Industries' Vice-President S. Ramakrishnan told Reuters, when asked for a response to the government's decision.
He said the group was still planning its response strategy.
SIA and Tata Industries Ltd submitted their proposal to launch a joint airline in February 1995. The Tatas planned to hold a 60 percent stake, with SIA owning the rest.
Since then, it has languished with the government, ensnared in a high-stakes battle over whether to permit foreign investment in the civil aviation sector.
"It's a bit too early to say what the next step will be," Ramakrishnan said. But he did not entirely rule out the possibility of salvaging the deal with Singapore Airlines in some form.
"We'd rather see what to do -- whether to fall in line or to to give up," he added.

Tuesday's decision appeared to be a victory for Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim, who has fought a high-profile battle to protect the state-owned airlines -- Indian Airlines on domestic routes and Air-India on international routes -- from foreign competition.

The cabinet also upheld a rule, set in January, limiting foreign firms which are not airlines to 40 percent equity stakes in domestic airlines. Non-resident Indians can hold stakes of up to 100 percent.
Foreign investors, whether or not they are airlines, which currently hold stakes in Indian airlines will have to conform to the rules.
Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways each have 20 percent stakes, valued at $4 million, in India's Jet Airways.
India began opening its aviation sector as part of an economic liberalisation programme launched under then prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991.
